item.stdout:
---
name: report-card
description: Emit a report card for any built unit — code feature, circuit block, subsystem, API, pipeline, signal chain — AND install the machinery that keeps it alive. A report card is the triad {.feature spec + .session conversation + RESULT (commits/PR/files)} born WITH the thing, graded honestly, linked both ways to its innards, and acting as the seed the work spawns from. Ships working tooling: an installer that drops card generators + self-stamping git hooks into any repo, so cards regenerate their own README/STATUS and stamp their own RESULT-LOGs. Use when building/shipping a unit that should carry its own durable, graded, session-backed description, or when a repo has no card system yet. Triggers on "report card", "report on this", "make a card for this", "card this feature/circuit", "whitelabel the card", "vibe diff", or finishing a unit of work that should self-document.
domain: cross-domain
version: 2.0.0
tags: [report-card, gherkin, feature, session, vibe-diff, wiki, traceability, electronics, circuits, honesty, seed, git-hooks, tooling]
---

# Report Card

> Building a unit of anything emits its report card. The card is not documentation
> bolted on after — it is the durable artifact the work is born with, the SEED the
> work spawns from, and the honest, graded, two-way-linked account of what the unit
> does and which of its innards do it. A unit shipped without its card is incomplete.

Domain-agnostic. The skin changes (Gherkin for code, circuit-block Given/When/Then
for electronics, request/response for an API); the skeleton never does.

**This skill ships working machinery, not just doctrine.** If a repo has no card
system, install it — don't hand-write prose that evaporates with the conversation.

---

## DO THIS FIRST — is the machinery present?

```bash
ls features/*.feature 2>/dev/null | head -3   # cards exist?
git config core.hooksPath                     # should print .githooks
```

**No cards / no hooks → install, then card.** One command, idempotent, never commits:

```bash
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh            # current repo, features/
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh --target /path/to/repo \
    --cards-dir features --title "Foo — Feature Reference"
```

It drops into the repo:

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `features/print-card.py` | cards → `README.md` + printable `dist/` |
| `features/gen-status.py` | cards → `STATUS.md` (the derived test matrix) |
| `features/gen-sessions.py` | Codex transcripts → `SESSIONS.generated.md` |
| `features/cards.conf` | per-repo knobs (title, source extensions, exclusions) |
| `features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt` | the house-style skeleton to copy |
| `features/INDEX.md` | the commit ⇄ card map (the one hand-kept file) |
| `.githooks/pre-commit` + `post-merge` + `report-card-stamp.sh` | the stamp engine |
| `.githooks/pre-commit.local` | repo-local jobs — **yours, never clobbered on reinstall** |
| `core.hooksPath = .githooks` | set for this clone (git won't auto-run committed hooks) |

Then, **every commit onward, with zero effort:** a diff touching a card's `# WATCH:`
symbols stamps a dated RESULT-LOG line into that card *in the same commit*, and a
staged card regenerates `STATUS.md` / `README.md` / `SESSIONS.generated.md` and stages
them too. Mapping is **by symbol, not filename** — touching an unrelated part of a
shared file does not tag every card.

Already installed elsewhere and want the engine refreshed? Re-run `install.sh`; it
overwrites the canonical hooks + generators and keeps `pre-commit.local`, `cards.conf`,
`INDEX.md`, and every card. `--force` to overwrite those too.

1. `cp features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt features/<name>.feature` and fill it in.

-  -- Boot sector with the 720K BIOS parameter block.
-  local vol_id = math.random(0, 65535) * 65536 + math.random(0, 65535)

    72	### What tells the two kinds of disk apart
    73	
    74	Measured against the real `TYPHOON 2000.IMA` from the NuEdge distribution:
    75	
    76	| Boot sector field | Typhoon/Cyclone-compatible disk | A Paketti data disk |
    77	|---|---|---|
    78	| OEM ID (offset 3) | `Y LM T8W` | `Y LM T8W` |
    79	| Extended boot signature (38) | `0x00` — short DOS 3.x BPB | `0x00` — short DOS 3.x BPB |
    80	| Volume label / FS type in boot sector | absent (that space is boot code or zero padding) | absent; the volume label lives in the root directory |
    81	| Boot code (62–509) | optional x86 message code | zero padding |
    82	| `0x55AA` at 510 | present on tested Cyclone images | present |
    83	| File attributes | `0x20` archive on tested Cyclone data disks | `0x20` archive |
    84	
    85	The x86 boot code on tested Cyclone data images is only for PCs — run on one it
    86	prints "This is a TX16W diskette / Insert a DOS diskette and press any key".
    87	The TX16W's own loader does not execute it, so Paketti keeps the compatible
    88	short BPB and OEM ID but leaves the boot-code area zero-filled. That is
    89	measured, not confirmed on hardware: no TX16W has been available to test it.

    92

    94	`BIG_DR_DISK2`) were verified before the boot-sector compatibility change:
    95	
    96	- `fsck_msdos` passes clean on all three, as it does on the real Typhoon disk.
    97	- All three mount natively on macOS with no repair prompt.
    98	- All 163 files across them are byte-identical to their sources.
    99	- Geometry is exactly 737,280 bytes, 80/2/9, 2 sectors per cluster, 112 root
   100	  entries, media 0xF9 — the same BPB the real Typhoon disk carries.
   101	
   102	So the filesystem is sound. What is untested is everything downstream of it:
   103	no image, voice or wave in this feature set has been read by a real TX16W.

   106	
   107	All three item types are big-endian IFF, and share a reference-chunk shape.
   108	
   109	```
   110	FORM <size> TYPV     .O## voice
   111	FORM <size> TYPP     .P## performance
   112	FORM <size> TYPS     .X## setup
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Reference chunks — `Wave` / `Voic` / `Perf`, always 20 bytes

+
+## Request
+
+Esa reported that Joshua says the Yamaha TX16W/Typhoon `.img` files exported by Paketti do not work. Esa also said Cyclone is installed in Renoise and asked whether there are `.img` files available to test, because a Paketti-created image should be transformable into something Cyclone can load.
+
+## Investigation
+
+No tracked `.img` files were found inside the Paketti tool repo. PakettiMCP is present in the repo and documents `http://localhost:19714/mcp`, but `curl` to `/health` and `tools/list` timed out from this shell, so live Renoise/Cyclone validation was not available during this pass.
+
+External known-good test material was downloaded from the Sonic Charge forum: `YAMAHA SYNTH ZONE.zip`, which contains `PROPHET5.img` and `SYMPHONI.img`. Both images are exactly 737,280 bytes and use the same core FAT12 geometry as Paketti: 512-byte sectors, 2 sectors per cluster, 1 reserved sector, 2 FATs, 112 root entries, 1440 total sectors, media byte `0xF9`, 3 sectors per FAT, 9 sectors per track, and 2 heads.
+
+The meaningful mismatch was the boot sector identity. Known-good Cyclone images use jump `EB 28 90`, OEM id `Y LM T8W`, and a short DOS 3.x BPB with no extended boot signature at byte 38. Paketti used jump `EB 3C 90`, OEM id `PAKETTI `, and an extended BPB with signature `0x29`, boot-sector volume label, and `FAT12` filesystem type string. The repo's own format note already identified the OEM/header shape as the plausible compatibility risk.
+
+## What Changed
